title: UK government's Consult tool analyses over 2,000 consultation responses with F1 of 0.76 against human reviewers
publisher: UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
summary: The Scottish Government used Consult, part of the UK government's Humphrey suite of AI tools, on a live consultation about regulating non-surgical cosmetic procedures, analysing over 2,000 responses across six qualitative questions; Scottish Government experts checked and refined the themes and, because this was the first live use, also manually reviewed every response. The first live evaluation gave an F1 score of 0.76 against the human analysis, with differences having a negligible effect on how themes were ranked; the government said more accuracy and efficiency testing would follow before any final rollout decision, projected savings of about 75,000 analyst days a year (20 million pounds) across 500 consultations, and said Consult would soon be used on major consultations without officials reviewing every response, with themes checked through an interactive dashboard.
